description: The drawing, editing, library and project-level commands of OrCAD Capture / OrCAD X Capture: placing schematic objects, managing parts and libraries, annotating and checking the design, and turning it into netlists, BOMs and printable or archivable output. Shortcut letters in parentheses are Capture's single-key accelerators, which work only when the schematic page editor has focus.

tools.name: Project Manager
tools.description: The tree window that represents an OrCAD project (.opj). It groups the design (.dsn) with its schematic folders and pages, the Design Cache, the configured libraries, PSpice simulation profiles and generated outputs. Almost every design-level command (Annotate, DRC, Create Netlist, BOM, Design Sync) is only enabled when a node is selected here, so scripts and users must select the .dsn node before invoking them.
tools.usage: File > Open > Project (.opj); the Project Manager window appears with File/Design Resources/Outputs folders
tools.example:
1. File > New > Project, choose 'PC Board Wizard'.
2. In the Project Manager expand Design Resources > design.dsn > SCHEMATIC1.
3. Double-click PAGE1 to open the page editor.
4. Select design.dsn, then Tools > Design Rules Check.
tools.notes: The .opj is a thin wrapper: deleting it loses library configuration and simulation profiles but not the schematic, which lives in the .dsn.

tools.name: New Project wizard
tools.description: Creates a project and asks which flow it targets: Analog or Mixed A/D (adds PSpice libraries and a simulation profile), PC Board Wizard (adds PCB-oriented libraries and enables netlisting to PCB Editor), Programmable Logic Wizard, or Schematic (drawing only). The choice sets the default library set and which menus are available, so picking the wrong one is the usual reason PSpice or PCB commands appear greyed out.
tools.usage: File > New > Project… > enter name, location and project type

parameters.name: Analog or Mixed A/D
parameters.description: Enables the PSpice menu, adds the PSpice symbol libraries and creates a simulation profile.

parameters.name: PC Board Wizard
parameters.description: Board-level flow: adds Discrete/Connector libraries and enables Create Netlist for PCB Editor and Design Sync.

parameters.name: Based upon an existing project
parameters.description: Clones an existing .opj as the starting point, carrying its library configuration across.

tools.example: File > New > Project > name 'ldo_reg', type 'Analog or Mixed A/D', location D:\work\ldo_reg, then choose 'Create a blank project'.

tools.name: Place Part
tools.description: Opens the Place Part panel to search the configured .olb libraries and drop a symbol on the page. Type a name or a wildcard in the Part box, pick the library, then click to place; each click drops another instance until Escape or right-click > End Mode. Parts placed here are copied into the Design Cache so the design stays self-contained.
tools.usage: Place > Part… (shortcut P)

parameters.name: Part
parameters.description: Name or wildcard pattern to search for, e.g. `R` or `LM*`.

parameters.name: Libraries
parameters.description: Which configured .olb files to search; Add Library (Alt+A) configures more.

parameters.name: Packaging
parameters.description: For multi-part packages, which section (A, B, C…) to place.

parameters.name: Part Search
parameters.description: Searches every .olb in a directory tree for a part name when you do not know which library holds it.

tools.example: Press P, type `R/ANALOG`, press Enter, click four times on the page to place R1..R4, press Esc.

tools.name: Place Wire
tools.description: Draws electrical connections between pins, other wires and ports. Click to start, click at each corner, and double-click or click on a pin to finish; Capture inserts junctions automatically where a wire endpoint meets another wire. Hold Shift while drawing for an unconstrained (any-angle) wire instead of the default orthogonal segments.
tools.usage: Place > Wire (shortcut W)
tools.example: Press W, click on U1 pin 1, click at the corner, click on R1 pin 2 — a net is created and a junction dot is added if the wire ends on an existing wire.
tools.notes: A wire that merely crosses another wire does not connect; only a junction (J) or an endpoint connection does.

tools.name: Place Bus
tools.description: Draws a bus, the thick line that carries a group of nets such as D[0..7]. A bus carries signals only through the net aliases of the wires entering it via bus entries, so the bus itself must be given a name like `ADDR[0..15]` with Place > Net Alias, and each branch wire must carry a matching member alias.
tools.usage: Place > Bus (shortcut B)
tools.example: Press B, draw the bus, press N and label it `D[0..7]`, then press E to add bus entries and N to alias each branch wire D0, D1, …
tools.notes: Bus naming is purely by alias — Capture does not check that a bus entry's wire alias is a member of the bus name, so mismatches silently create separate nets. Run DRC to catch them.

tools.name: Place Bus Entry
tools.description: Places the short 45-degree stub that visually attaches a wire to a bus. It is a graphical element: connectivity still comes from the net alias on the attached wire matching a member of the bus name. Press R while placing to flip the entry's direction.
tools.usage: Place > Bus Entry (shortcut E)
tools.example: Press E, click next to the bus to drop the entry, then press W to draw the branch wire and N to alias it `D3`.

tools.name: Place Junction
tools.description: Adds or removes a connection dot where wires cross. Capture places junctions automatically at T connections, but crossing wires are deliberately not connected, so an explicit junction is needed to join them. Clicking an existing junction removes it.
tools.usage: Place > Junction (shortcut J)
tools.example: Press J and click the intersection of the VCC wire and the decoupling-cap wire to tie them together.

tools.name: Place Net Alias
tools.description: Gives a wire or bus an explicit net name instead of Capture's generated N00xxx name. Two unconnected wires that carry the same alias on the same page are merged into one net, which is how buses and long signals are wired without drawing. Aliases are also what appear in netlists and what PCB Editor and PSpice use for net names.
tools.usage: Place > Net Alias… (shortcut N), then click the wire to attach the label

parameters.name: Alias
parameters.description: The net name; a trailing number auto-increments on each subsequent placement.

parameters.name: Color / Rotation / Font
parameters.description: Display properties of the label only.

tools.example: Press N, type `SCL`, OK, then click the I2C clock wire on each page where it appears.
tools.notes: Aliases only merge nets within the same schematic page. Use off-page connectors or hierarchical ports to cross pages.

tools.name: Place Power / Place Ground
tools.description: Places a power or ground symbol whose Name property becomes a global net name that connects across every page of the design without wiring. Ground symbols (GND, GND_EARTH, 0 for PSpice) and power symbols (VCC, VDD, VCC_BAR, VCC_CIRCLE) come from CAPSYM.OLB or the PSpice SOURCE libraries; only the Name matters electrically, the graphic is cosmetic.
tools.usage: Place > Power (shortcut F) / Place > Ground (shortcut G)
tools.example: Press G, pick `0/SOURCE` for PSpice ground (node 0 is mandatory for simulation), place it on the return net.
tools.notes: For PSpice the analog reference must be net `0`; using a GND symbol named GND without connecting it to 0 produces 'Node is floating' errors.

tools.name: Place Off-Page Connector
tools.description: Connects nets of the same name between pages that are at the same level of a flat design. Two off-page connectors with identical names on different pages form one net. Use them for flat multi-page designs; hierarchical designs use ports and blocks instead.
tools.usage: Place > Off-Page Connector…
tools.example: On page 1 place OFFPAGELEFT-R named `RESET_N`; on page 2 place the same connector with the same name to continue the net.

tools.name: Place Hierarchical Block / Port / Pin
tools.description: Builds a hierarchical design. A hierarchical block is a rectangle on a parent page that references a child schematic folder; hierarchical pins on the block's edge must match by name the hierarchical ports placed inside the child schematic. Use Design > Descend Hierarchy (or Shift+I) to open the child. Repeating the same block name creates multiple instances of one circuit.
tools.usage: Place > Hierarchical Block…, Place > Hierarchical Port…, Place > Hierarchical Pin…

parameters.name: Reference
parameters.description: The instance name of the block, used to build the flattened reference designators.

parameters.name: Implementation Type
parameters.description: Schematic View for a child schematic; also supports VHDL, Verilog, EDIF and PSpice models.

parameters.name: Implementation Name
parameters.description: Name of the child schematic folder the block points at.

tools.example: Place a block named `FILTER1` with Implementation Name `RC_FILTER`, add pins IN/OUT, then inside RC_FILTER place ports IN and OUT.
tools.notes: Pin and port names must match exactly, including case. A mismatch is reported by DRC as an unconnected hierarchical pin.

tools.name: Place No Connect
tools.description: Marks a pin as deliberately unused so that DRC stops reporting it as unconnected and the netlister omits it. The X marker is attached to the pin, not to the page, so it moves with the part.
tools.usage: Place > No Connect (shortcut X), then click each unused pin
tools.example: Press X and click the four unused GPIO pins on U3; re-run Tools > Design Rules Check and the warnings disappear.

tools.name: Place Text / Line / Polyline / Rectangle / Ellipse / Arc
tools.description: Non-electrical annotation graphics. Text (Shift+T) adds free comments, and the Place > Line/Polyline/Rectangle/Ellipse/Arc commands draw decoration such as function boundaries and notes. None of these create connectivity, which is the usual trap: a 'wire' drawn with Line looks right but nets nothing.
tools.usage: Place > Text (Shift+T), Place > Line, Place > Polyline, Place > Rectangle, Place > Ellipse, Place > Arc
tools.example: Shift+T, type 'Do not populate R17 on Rev A', place next to the part.
tools.notes: Graphics drawn on the page are page-local; graphics that should appear on every page belong in the Design Template or title block.

tools.name: Title Block
tools.description: Places the drawing frame's title block from CAPSYM.OLB or a custom library. Its fields (Title, Document Number, Revision, Organization Name, Address lines) are properties that can be edited per page, or set for the whole design from Options > Design Template > Title Block so new pages inherit them.
tools.usage: Place > Title Block…; defaults at Options > Design Template > Title Block
tools.example: Options > Design Template > Title Block, fill Title/Organization/Revision, then every new page is created with those values.

tools.name: Part Editor
tools.description: The symbol editor for library parts. Opened by double-clicking a part in a .olb, or by right-clicking a placed part > Edit Part (which edits only the cached copy) . It draws the body with Place > Rectangle/Line/Arc and adds pins with Place > Pin or Place > Pin Array, sets Pin Type (Input, Output, Bidirectional, Open Collector, Passive, Power, 3-State), Shape (Line, Clock, Dot, Short, Zero-length) and pin visibility.
tools.usage: Double-click a part in a library, or right-click a placed part > Edit Part (Ctrl+E on the cached copy)

parameters.name: Pin Type
parameters.description: Electrical type used by DRC's connection matrix (Input, Output, Bidirectional, Power, Passive, Open Emitter/Collector, 3 State).

parameters.name: PinNumber / PinName
parameters.description: Physical package pin number and the logical name shown inside the body.

parameters.name: Parts per Pkg
parameters.description: Number of homogeneous or heterogeneous sections in the package (e.g. 4 for a quad op-amp).

tools.example: Open MYLIB.OLB, File > New Part, name 'LM324', Parts per Pkg = 4, draw the triangle, Place > Pin for +IN/-IN/OUT, then File > Save.
tools.notes: Editing a placed part edits the Design Cache copy only; use Design > Update Cache or Replace Cache to push library changes into an existing design.

tools.name: Design Cache
tools.description: The node in the Project Manager holding a private copy of every symbol used in the design, so the .dsn opens correctly even without the original libraries. Right-click it for Update Cache (re-read symbols from the configured libraries), Cleanup Cache (drop unused symbols) and Replace Cache (swap one part for another everywhere).
tools.usage: Project Manager > Design Resources > design.dsn > Design Cache; right-click for Update/Cleanup/Replace Cache
tools.example: After fixing a pin number in MYLIB.OLB: right-click Design Cache > Update Cache, then re-run DRC.
tools.notes: A stale cache is the most common cause of 'the library is right but the schematic is wrong'.

tools.name: Library configuration (Add/Remove Library, New Library)
tools.description: Controls which .olb files Capture searches when placing parts. Libraries are added per project from the Place Part panel's Add Library button, and created with File > New > Library. The Project Manager's Library folder shows the current list; order matters when two libraries define the same part name.
tools.usage: Place > Part > Add Library (Alt+A) / Remove Library; File > New > Library
tools.example: Place Part panel > Add Library > browse to D:\libs\company.olb; the parts become searchable immediately.

tools.name: Part Search
tools.description: Scans a directory tree of .olb files for a part name or wildcard, without the library having to be configured first. Results show the library path so it can be added with one click. Indispensable when you know a device name but not which of the hundreds of shipped libraries holds it.
tools.usage: Place > Part panel > Part Search button (magnifier), enter a name/wildcard and a search path
tools.example: Search for `74*245*` under C:\Cadence\...\tools\capture\library to find the buffer in TTL.OLB.

tools.name: Property Editor (Edit Properties)
tools.description: A spreadsheet view of every property on the selected objects — parts, pins, nets, pages or the whole design. Rows are objects, columns are properties; New Property adds a column, Display controls whether a property is shown on the schematic, and Filter switches between property sets (Orcad-Capture, Orcad-PSpice, Orcad-Layout, Current properties). It is the fastest way to bulk-edit values, footprints and DNI flags, and it supports copy/paste to and from Excel.
tools.usage: Select objects > Edit > Properties… (Ctrl+E on selection), or right-click > Edit Properties

parameters.name: New Property
parameters.description: Adds a user property column, e.g. `MPN`, `Tolerance`, `DNI`.

parameters.name: Display
parameters.description: Sets how the property appears on the page: Do Not Display, Value Only, Name and Value, Both if Value Exists.

parameters.name: Filter by
parameters.description: Limits the visible columns to a property set such as Orcad-PSpice or Orcad-Layout.

tools.example: Select all resistors (Edit > Find, type=Part, value R*), Ctrl+E, paste a column of PCB Footprint values from Excel, close the editor.
tools.notes: Properties edited at instance level override the Design Cache/library value; the cell colour indicates the source.

tools.name: Find (Edit > Find)
tools.description: Searches the whole design for parts, nets, pins, ports, off-page connectors, text, bookmarks and DRC markers by name or wildcard. Results list the page and can be double-clicked to jump and select the object. It is the practical tool for locating where a net is used across a multi-page design.
tools.usage: Edit > Find… (Ctrl+F), enter a string, tick the object classes to search
tools.example: Ctrl+F, search `VBUS`, tick Nets and Power — every page carrying the net is listed.

tools.name: Browse (Parts, Nets, DRC Markers…)
tools.description: Generates a flat, sortable report window of a chosen object class for the whole design: Parts, Nets, Flat Nets, Pins, Title Blocks, Bookmarks, DRC Markers, Off-Page Connectors, Ports and Libraries. Double-clicking a row cross-probes to the schematic. Reports can be saved to a text file, which makes Browse a quick ad-hoc export when a full BOM is overkill.
tools.usage: Select the .dsn in the Project Manager > Edit > Browse > <object class>
tools.example: Edit > Browse > DRC Markers to get one list of every DRC error with its page and location.

tools.name: Annotate
tools.description: Assigns reference designators to parts. It can annotate the whole design or just selected pages, reset all designators to their U? form, add intersheet references, or renumber incrementally so that only new parts get numbers. Packaging options control how multi-section parts (a quad NAND) are combined into physical packages, and the ordering options control whether numbering runs left-to-right or top-to-bottom.
tools.usage: Select design.dsn in Project Manager > Tools > Annotate…

parameters.name: Update entire design / selection
parameters.description: Scope of the operation.

parameters.name: Incremental reference update
parameters.description: Only unannotated (U?) parts get numbers; existing designators are kept.

parameters.name: Unconditional reference update
parameters.description: Renumbers everything from scratch — never do this after the board is laid out.

parameters.name: Reset part references to '?'
parameters.description: Clears all designators.

parameters.name: Combined property string
parameters.description: Controls which properties must match for two sections to be packaged together.

tools.example: Tools > Annotate > scope 'Update entire design', action 'Incremental reference update', Physical Packaging 'Combined property string = {Value}{Source Package}', OK.
tools.notes: Always use incremental annotation once a PCB exists; an unconditional renumber breaks the link to the board and forces a full re-place.

tools.name: Back Annotate
tools.description: Applies reference designator and gate/pin swap changes that were made in the PCB layout back into the schematic, using a swap file (.swp) produced by PCB Editor or OrCAD Layout. This keeps the schematic and board consistent after the layout engineer renumbers parts or swaps equivalent gates and pins for routability.
tools.usage: Select design.dsn > Tools > Back Annotate…, choose the PCB Editor/Layout tab and the .swp file
tools.example: In PCB Editor run File > Export > Logic (feedback), then in Capture Tools > Back Annotate > PCB Editor > select board.swp > OK.
tools.notes: In the OrCAD X flow, Design Sync replaces the file-based forward/back annotation loop.

tools.name: Design Rules Check (DRC)
tools.description: Checks electrical and structural correctness of the schematic: unconnected pins and nets, duplicate references, mismatched hierarchical ports, illegal pin-to-pin connections driven by the ERC connection matrix, off-page connector mismatches and missing properties. Results are written to a report and optionally placed as DRC markers on the pages. It must be clean before netlisting.
tools.usage: Select design.dsn > Tools > Design Rules Check…

parameters.name: Run Electrical Rules / Physical Rules
parameters.description: Chooses connectivity checks versus structural checks such as duplicate references.

parameters.name: Create DRC markers for warnings
parameters.description: Draws markers on the schematic in addition to the text report.

parameters.name: ERC Matrix tab
parameters.description: The pin-type-versus-pin-type matrix that decides which connections are errors, warnings or legal.

parameters.name: Report File
parameters.description: Path of the .drc text report.

tools.example: Tools > Design Rules Check > check 'Create DRC markers', 'Check single node nets', 'Check unconnected nets' > OK, then Edit > Browse > DRC Markers to review.

tools.name: Create Netlist
tools.description: Exports the connectivity to another tool. Tabs select the format: PCB Editor (writes pstchip.dat/pstxnet.dat/pstxprt.dat for Allegro/OrCAD PCB Editor), Layout (.mnl), PSpice (.net/.cir), EDIF 2 0 0, VHDL, Verilog, INF, SPICE, plus a large set of third-party formats under 'Other'. Capture runs DRC first and refuses to netlist a design with errors.
tools.usage: Select design.dsn > Tools > Create Netlist…, choose the tab for the target tool

parameters.name: PCB Editor tab
parameters.description: Produces the three pst*.dat logic files plus a board directory; 'Create PCB Editor Netlist' and 'Setup' control the property mapping.

parameters.name: PSpice tab
parameters.description: Writes the simulation netlist; normally invoked implicitly by PSpice > Run.

parameters.name: Other tab
parameters.description: Uses a formatter .dll/.cf combination for EDIF, Protel, Tango, Cadstar, PADS and similar formats.

parameters.name: Combined property string
parameters.description: Template such as `{PCB Footprint}` that maps schematic properties into the netlist's part field.

tools.example: Tools > Create Netlist > PCB Editor tab > Netlist Files directory 'allegro' > tick 'Create or Update PCB Editor Board (Netrev)' > OK.
tools.notes: In OrCAD X the preferred path is PCB > Design Sync, which keeps a live incremental link instead of regenerating flat netlist files.

tools.name: Bill of Materials
tools.description: Generates a parts list from the design's properties. A header/combined-property template controls the columns ({Item}\t{Quantity}\t{Reference}\t{Value}), and options merge identical parts, include or exclude parts marked Do Not Populate, and open the result in Excel. CIS-enabled projects get a much richer Standard/Variant BOM driven by the linked database instead.
tools.usage: Select design.dsn > Tools > Bill of Materials…

parameters.name: Header / Combined property string
parameters.description: Tab-separated template defining the report columns.

parameters.name: Place each part entry on a separate line
parameters.description: Disables grouping of identical parts.

parameters.name: Open in Excel
parameters.description: Launches Excel on the generated file and can apply a template.

parameters.name: Include File
parameters.description: Merges extra non-schematic line items (hardware, labels) into the list.

tools.example: Tools > Bill of Materials, Combined property string `{Item}\t{Quantity}\t{Reference}\t{Value}\t{MPN}`, output bom.bom, OK.

tools.name: Cross Reference Parts
tools.description: Reports where every physical package's sections live — which page and coordinates each gate of a multi-part package was placed on — and optionally the reverse view listing parts per page. It is the report to run before repackaging or when hunting down the fourth section of a quad gate.
tools.usage: Select design.dsn > Tools > Cross Reference…
tools.example: Tools > Cross Reference > 'Cross reference all parts', 'Report the X and Y coordinates of all parts' > OK.

tools.name: Export / Import Properties
tools.description: Round-trips design properties through a tab-delimited text file. Export Properties writes every part, pin and net property to a file that can be edited in Excel; Import Properties reads it back and applies the changes. This is the bulk-edit path when the Property Editor spreadsheet is impractical, e.g. filling manufacturer part numbers for a whole design.
tools.usage: Select design.dsn > Tools > Export Properties… / Tools > Import Properties…
tools.example: Tools > Export Properties > props.txt, edit the MPN column in Excel, Tools > Import Properties > props.txt.
tools.notes: Only properties that already exist as columns are exported; add the property once in the Property Editor first.

tools.name: Update Properties
tools.description: Applies a property update file to selected parts or the whole design, used to push library or database changes such as revised footprints onto existing instances. It is a lighter-weight alternative to replacing parts through the Design Cache.
tools.usage: Select design.dsn > Tools > Update Properties…
tools.example: Prepare an update file mapping Value to a new PCB Footprint, then Tools > Update Properties > select the file > OK.

tools.name: Design Difference Viewer
tools.description: Compares two Capture designs or two revisions of the same design and reports added, deleted and modified pages, parts, nets and properties, with the differences highlighted graphically. Use it for design reviews, for confirming what a colleague changed, and for validating an ECO before it reaches the board.
tools.usage: Accessories/Tools > Design Difference Viewer (shipped as a Capture utility), select the two .dsn files
tools.example: Launch the Design Difference Viewer, pick rev_a.dsn and rev_b.dsn, run the comparison and review the net and property change list.

tools.name: Design Sync (PCB > Design Sync)
tools.description: The OrCAD X replacement for file-based forward/back annotation. It keeps Capture and the PCB Editor / Presto board in a live incremental relationship: changes are compared, listed as a set of ECOs, and applied in either direction after review. Unlike Create Netlist it never regenerates the whole board, so placement and routing survive.
tools.usage: PCB menu > Design Sync (OrCAD X Capture); the PCB must be associated with the project first
tools.example: PCB > Design Sync > review the list of added/removed components and nets > Apply to push the changes to the board.
tools.notes: Available in OrCAD X / 23.1 and later. Older releases use Tools > Create Netlist plus Tools > Back Annotate.

tools.name: Zoom, Pan and Fit
tools.description: View navigation in the page editor. I zooms in, O zooms out, C centres on the cursor, and View > Zoom > All (or Ctrl+Shift+Home) fits the page. The mouse wheel scrolls, Ctrl+wheel zooms and the middle button pans, so most navigation never needs the menu.
tools.usage: I (zoom in), O (zoom out), C (centre), View > Zoom > All, View > Zoom > Area
tools.example: Press O twice to see the whole sheet, C over the connector to centre on it, then I to zoom back in.

tools.name: Grid and Snap to Grid
tools.description: Controls the schematic grid display and whether objects snap to it. Capture's connectivity grid is fixed at 0.1 inch for pins, so snap should normally stay on — a part placed off-grid will not connect to wires even though the drawing looks correct. View > Grid toggles visibility and View > Snap to Grid toggles the snap.
tools.usage: View > Grid, View > Snap to Grid; styles at Options > Preferences > Grid Display
tools.example: Options > Preferences > Grid Display > Schematic Page Grid: Dots, Grid spacing 'Pointer snap to grid' ticked.
tools.notes: If a wire refuses to connect to a pin, the part is almost always off-grid; select it and use Edit > Properties to reset its Location, or cut and re-place with snap on.

tools.name: Schematic Page Properties / Design Template
tools.description: Sets the drawing sheet size (A–E, A4–A0 or custom), border, grid reference and title block. Options > Schematic Page Properties changes only the open page; Options > Design Template sets the defaults used for every new page along with fonts, title block text, page size and the parts-per-page grid references.
tools.usage: Options > Schematic Page Properties…; Options > Design Template…
tools.example: Options > Design Template > Page Size > tick Inches, select B (11 x 17), Grid Reference: Horizontal 5 / Vertical 4, then add new pages.

tools.name: Print / Print Preview
tools.description: Prints selected pages or the whole design with control over scale, fit-to-page, print quality and whether a single page or the entire schematic folder is sent. Print Preview shows the paginated result. Combined with a PDF printer or the dedicated PDF export it is how review packages are produced.
tools.usage: File > Print… (Ctrl+P), File > Print Preview, File > Print Setup
tools.example: Select the SCHEMATIC1 folder in the Project Manager, File > Print, tick 'Scale to paper size', Print range: All, OK.

tools.name: Export as PDF
tools.description: Writes a hyperlinked, searchable PDF of the schematic without a third-party printer driver. Options generate bookmarks per page, make net and part names selectable text, and create hyperlinks so that clicking an off-page connector or hierarchical block jumps to the target page — the standard way to share a design for review.
tools.usage: File > Export > PDF… (or File > Print with the Capture PDF writer)

parameters.name: Output File
parameters.description: Destination .pdf.

parameters.name: Create Net and Part Hyperlinks / Bookmarks
parameters.description: Adds navigation between pages and a page bookmark tree.

parameters.name: Page Size / Orientation
parameters.description: Paper size and rotation for the exported sheets.

tools.example: File > Export > PDF, tick 'Generate Net and Part Hyperlinks' and 'Create Bookmarks', output review.pdf.

tools.name: Export DXF / Import DXF
tools.description: Exchanges the schematic graphics with AutoCAD-style DXF. Export writes the page geometry as DXF entities for mechanical documentation; Import brings a DXF drawing in as Capture graphic objects (no connectivity is created). Useful for company drawing frames and for putting a schematic into a mechanical drawing set.
tools.usage: File > Export > DXF…; File > Import > DXF…
tools.example: File > Export > DXF, select the page, set units to inches, write page1.dxf.

tools.name: Archive Project
tools.description: Collects the .opj, .dsn, every referenced .olb, PSpice models and generated outputs into a single self-contained folder or zip, so the project can be moved or handed over without broken library paths. This is the correct way to send a Capture design to someone else — copying only the .dsn leaves the recipient with an un-editable Design Cache.
tools.usage: Right-click the project in the Project Manager > Archive Project…
tools.example: Right-click ldo_reg.opj > Archive Project > tick 'Archive design and library files', destination D:\handoff\ldo_reg.zip.

tools.name: Cross-probing to PCB / PSpice
tools.description: Links selections between Capture and the other tools: selecting a part or net in the schematic highlights the corresponding component or net in PCB Editor, and PSpice markers placed on the schematic determine which waveforms Probe displays. It is enabled per session and is the main navigation aid when debugging layout or simulation results against the schematic.
tools.usage: Open both tools on the same design; in PCB Editor use Edit > Cross Probe or the Capture 'Enable cross-probing' option
tools.example: With PCB Editor open, click net DDR_CK in Capture — the corresponding rat/trace is highlighted on the board.

tools.name: Undo / Redo and Repeat
tools.description: Multi-level undo (Ctrl+Z) and redo (Ctrl+Y) of schematic edits, plus F4 to repeat the last placement command. Undo depth is configurable in Options > Preferences > Miscellaneous. Note that project-level operations such as Annotate and netlist generation are outside the undo stack.
tools.usage: Edit > Undo (Ctrl+Z), Edit > Redo (Ctrl+Y), Edit > Repeat (F4)
tools.example: Place a decoupling capacitor, press F4 repeatedly to drop the same part again at each click point.
tools.notes: Annotate cannot be undone — save (or use incremental annotation) before running it.
